nodes.description: Because Rab3/Rab27-dependent regulated secretion underlies hormone and exocrine-gland output, MADD deficiency produces combined endocrine and exocrine dysfunction. Reported manifestations include dysregulated glucose homeostasis (neonatal hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia), hypopituitarism with growth hormone and gonadotropin deficiency, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency contributing to chronic diarrhea and poor weight gain, and other gland involvement. MADD-deficient stem-cell-derived pancreatic islets show reduced beta-cell number, decreased insulin content, and an increased proinsulin-to-insulin ratio.

nodes.description: MADD/DENN exhibits guanine-nucleotide exchange factor activity toward neuronal Rab3 isoforms (Rab3A, Rab3B, Rab3C, Rab3D) that regulate calcium-dependent neurotransmitter exocytosis and KIF1A/KIF1B-beta-mediated presynaptic vesicle transport. Patient-derived DENN-domain missense variants (such as P372L in severe Group 1 disease and L346P in predominantly neurological Group 2 disease) abolish recruitment and activation of Rab3A, Rab3B, and Rab3D, impairing synaptic neurotransmission underlying global developmental delay, hypotonia, and seizures.

nodes.description: MADD is a DENN-domain guanine-nucleotide exchange factor that activates Rab3 and Rab27 (and additional Rab substrates such as Rab8B, Rab15, Rab26, Rab37). Loss of MADD impairs Rab-dependent membrane trafficking and regulated secretion/endocytosis; patient cells show a defect in endocytosis of epidermal growth factor. Because Rab3/Rab27-dependent regulated exocytosis underlies neurotransmitter, hormone, and other secretory-granule release, this trafficking defect propagates to secretory tissues. Different missense alleles impair Rab activation to different degrees, offering a mechanistic basis for the severity spectrum (see the P372L/L346P evidence below).
